status_history.reason: Calibration-only draft adapting an upstream prompt-compilation method into a 16:9 HyperFrames editorial-print profile. It has no production render evidence, is not default-selectable, and must remain author-calibration-only until current HyperFrames render and positive/negative example review pass.

title: Quiet Editorial Print — Calibration Only
summary: A draft 16:9 flat editorial-print compiler that requires one frozen ordinary-primary asset per shot in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order, allocates negative space by semantic density, keeps HTML/SVG typography and marks auxiliary, limits each shot to one semantic anchor and one high-chroma accent, and lets at most paper plus one reproduction process cause the motion.
best_for: one conclusion, definition, principle, or short approved quotation
one evidence fragment, correction, or before-to-after state
reflective writing, archival interpretation, reading, and cultural research with verified source copy
quiet section breaks that convert a dense argument into one readable judgment
shots with one routed ordinary-primary paper, print, photo, scan, or specimen source and concise factual HTML/SVG annotations
avoid_for: real-time monitoring, multi-node networks, or complex process diagrams
more than six independent facts that must remain visible at once
product UI operation, code execution, map navigation, or spatial demonstrations
multi-subject performance, immersive environments, or camera-space storytelling
commercial calls to action, price promotions, logo showcases, or fixed brand-ad layouts
requests that depend on an image generator accurately drawing factual text, tables, numbers, or marks

canvas.tone: quiet, low-reflectance editorial paper field with legible black-gray ink and one decisive chromatic signal
canvas.background_policy: Fill the 16:9 frame with one opaque, orthographic support field. The shot's visible material presence comes from one frozen ordinary-primary asset—either a paper/print/scan field or an inset photo/specimen—resolved in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order. HTML/CSS/SVG may supply a plain support fill, crop, typography, marks, and auxiliary texture, but can never be the sole or primary material. Use no simulated camera, page mockup, cast shadow, or spatial staging.

palette.strategy: Paper neutrals and black-gray ink support exactly one high-chroma hue selected from user/project evidence when available. The accent owns one semantic role and remains saturated through any permitted reproduction process.

roles.semantic: quiet reading field and semantic pause
roles.value_policy: warm or cool off-white at low chroma, low-reflectance, opaque, and lower contrast than all factual type

roles.semantic: factual statement, name, value, quotation, or evidence
roles.value_policy: near-black or dark neutral ink with target-raster readable contrast

roles.semantic: source, qualifier, unit, annotation, or structural rule
roles.value_policy: mid-gray neutral ink, visibly subordinate but never too faint to verify

roles.semantic: the shot's single current claim, correction, or semantic anchor
roles.value_policy: Prefer one high-chroma hue evidenced by user, brand, or approved source media. When none exists, the Director selects one content-driven semantic hue and records why it maps to the claim, correction, or anchor. Keep it opaque, typically about 1.5%-5% of the 16:9 frame or 15%-35% of the anchor, and distinct at thumbnail scale; never fall back to a default purple-blue gradient or introduce a second competing hue.

roles.purpose: carry the approved conclusion, definition, quotation, or primary value
roles.style_relation: largest factual voice, real HTML text or SVG text, high contrast, and fully readable during the hold

roles.purpose: carry approved supporting facts, qualifiers, units, or a concise source fragment
roles.style_relation: smaller serif or typewriter-like role aligned to the anchor edge or a narrow editorial column

roles.purpose: carry only real source, sequence, date, location, or identifier metadata when supplied
roles.style_relation: smallest locally verified mono or serif role; omitted rather than fabricated when no metadata exists

typography.local_fallback_policy: Bind project-local font files only and verify actual Latin/CJK/numeric glyph coverage. Never use remote fonts or system/generic fallback. All factual characters remain DOM/SVG text and are never delegated to an image generator.

materials: exactly one frozen ordinary-primary asset per shot, resolved in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order and visibly contributing pixels in the result region
the ordinary-primary asset supplies the paper, print, photo, scan, or specimen material; HTML/CSS/SVG supplies only real typography, structure, marks, crop geometry, and auxiliary texture
paper is material-process one and at most one optional reproduction process may be chosen from scan noise, halftone, slight misregistration, or ink bleed
spatial_hierarchy: density-banded negative space establishes the reading pause
one routed ordinary-primary material remains visibly present and supplies the shot's material ground
one semantic anchor carries the shot's unique judgment
real statement typography names or may become the semantic focus while remaining auxiliary to the ordinary-primary material
evidence and folio text remain subordinate and verifiable
one high-chroma accent identifies the active semantic role
visual_system.whitespace_policy: Select whitespace from semantic density rather than a fixed poster percentage: low density 58%-72%, medium 44%-58%, high 30%-44%. Low permits one statement and one note; medium permits one statement and at most two support groups; high permits two to three structured text bands but still one main anchor. Split the shot or select another profile when more than six independent facts would require smaller unreadable type.

focus_policy.rule: Exactly one semantic anchor owns each shot, and exactly one ordinary-primary asset supplies its visible material ground. If typography is the semantic focus, the routed paper/print/scan asset remains the ordinary primary and no second image subject is added. If a specimen or evidence fragment is the semantic focus, that routed asset is the ordinary primary and typography only names, qualifies, or verifies it.

purposes: state one conclusion, definition, principle, or approved short quotation
turn a dense preceding argument into one readable editorial judgment
scene_grammar.composition: Bind one ordinary-primary paper, print, or scan asset through user-media → image-generation → Pexels and keep its material pixels visibly present across the page. Real HTML/SVG statement type is the single semantic focus, placed in one offset field with density-banded negative space. A short real source or qualifier may sit on the same baseline system. One high-chroma keyword or rule marks the current claim; no second image subject is added.
required_semantics: one approved sentence or value that can stand as the shot's conclusion
a meaningful reason for the selected word, phrase, or rule to receive the chromatic emphasis
one frozen ordinary-primary paper, print, or scan asset with route, asset identity, provenance, and visible result-region contribution
forbidden_uses: inventing a poetic phrase, citation, date, or identifier to fill empty space
asking an image generator to render the sentence
using HTML/CSS/SVG typography or procedural paper texture as the sole or primary material
omitting the ordinary-primary asset because the shot is type-led
adding an unrelated photo, object, or decorative microtext cluster
chaining centered title cards across adjacent shots

purposes: make one routed concrete object, symbol, approved photo crop, print, or scan carry an abstract idea
pair one rights-cleared visual specimen with concise factual annotation
scene_grammar.composition: Resolve one ordinary-primary specimen asset in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order and place it in a left, right, upper, lower, or centered island. Keep its pixels within the selected density-tier anchor share and away from frame edges. One HTML/SVG statement and optional evidence note press against or point toward that asset; native vectors may crop, frame, or mark it but cannot replace it. The accent belongs to the specimen or one annotation, never both as competing foci.
required_semantics: one real or clearly interpretable specimen with a direct mapping to the narration
one frozen ordinary-primary asset with route, asset identity, provenance, and visible result-region contribution
forbidden_uses: a collage of unrelated clippings, stickers, or objects
a full-bleed photographic scene
generic stock-photo realism with no semantic mapping
a native SVG object, icon, or procedural shape acting as the sole or primary material
two coequal specimens or a specimen plus a type anchor of equal strength

purposes: show one verifiable quotation, document fragment, number, or source excerpt
make a correction, qualification, or evidence-based judgment visible
scene_grammar.composition: Bind one ordinary-primary evidence or paper material in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order. When source appearance is itself factual evidence, user-media must supply the verified crop; generated or stock material cannot impersonate that evidence. Re-typeset approved factual content as HTML/SVG when legibility is required, while keeping the routed ordinary material visibly present. The surrounding page remains quiet and the accent marks one verified clause, value, or correction.
required_semantics: a real source fragment supplied or approved for use
enough source context to avoid turning the fragment into a misleading decorative quote
one frozen ordinary-primary asset with route, asset identity, provenance, and visible result-region contribution
forbidden_uses: fabricated archival metadata or a fake document facsimile
generated or stock imagery presented as factual source evidence
a pure HTML/SVG page with no ordinary-primary material bound
unreadable raster text standing in for a factual claim
multiple source fragments arranged as a scrapbook
highlighting a clause that is not supported by the source

purposes: show one concept moving from input to result
visualize correction, alignment, confirmation, diffusion, or clarification through a print-process cause
scene_grammar.composition: Resolve one ordinary-primary paper, print, photo, scan, or specimen asset in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order. The same routed material changes state in place or through one directional feed. Entry shows the initial state briefly, one print-causal action produces the result, and the final state replaces rather than sits beside the initial state. Real HTML/SVG type and marks label or structure the state but never replace the ordinary-primary material.
required_semantics: one identifiable subject with a meaningful initial and final state
a print-process action whose physical behavior maps to the narrated change
one frozen ordinary-primary asset with route, asset identity, provenance, and visible result-region contribution
forbidden_uses: decorative process animation with no state change
a native-only state diagram or typographic transformation with no ordinary-primary material
simultaneous before-and-after panels acting as two anchors
perpetual jitter, paper drift, or moving texture during the reading hold
using ink bleed for content that has no spread, absorption, or boundary-change meaning

entries.semantic_trigger: A conclusion, name, value, or short quotation becomes confirmed and should settle as the stable result.
entries.action: Over the frozen ordinary-primary paper, print, or scan asset, a single horizontal or vertical pressure boundary advances across the semantic anchor while real HTML/SVG glyphs move from light impression to stable ink. No characters are generated as pixels and the native action never replaces the routed material.
entries.result_state: The complete approved statement is fully readable in stable ink, the pressure boundary is gone, and the ordinary-primary material remains visibly present.
entries.hold_policy: Complete the impression before the reading hold; remove all pressure motion for the remainder of the SRT window.

entries.semantic_trigger: The narration advances to one new piece of evidence, one next step, or a section boundary that behaves like a sheet feed.
entries.action: One flat feed edge moves along the reading direction and reveals the destination shot's frozen ordinary-primary material plus its real typeset copy. The previous routed material leaves as one page state rather than fragmenting into pieces.
entries.result_state: The new ordinary-primary material visibly contributes to the full-frame page, the feed edge has exited, and one semantic anchor remains.
entries.hold_policy: Use the feed only during entry or exit; never keep the page moving while the text is being read.

entries.semantic_trigger: Two descriptions are corrected, aligned, normalized, or brought into agreement on the same subject.
entries.action: A short auxiliary chromatic impression of the same routed ordinary-primary anchor begins slightly offset and deterministically aligns with its primary material position.
entries.result_state: The single ordinary-primary anchor is visibly registered, remains materially present, and the corrected HTML/SVG statement holds without jitter.
entries.hold_policy: The offset exists only during the correction action. Use at most once per section and never as ambient texture.

entries.semantic_trigger: A real but initially indistinct piece of evidence becomes identifiable or measurable.
entries.action: A deterministic auxiliary SVG/CSS screening mask changes from coarse cells to the final readable treatment of the frozen ordinary-primary asset while the factual annotation remains real text.
entries.result_state: The routed ordinary-primary evidence asset and its real annotation are clear, stable, visibly contributing, and inspectable.
entries.hold_policy: Stop screen changes before the hold and retain a static final pattern; do not animate grain continuously.

entries.semantic_trigger: The narration explicitly describes spread, absorption, diffusion, reach, or a changing boundary.
entries.action: One controlled auxiliary ink boundary expands from the semantic origin across the frozen ordinary-primary material and reveals or recolors the same anchor along a defined direction.
entries.result_state: The ordinary-primary material remains visible; the new boundary and affected region are stable, bounded, and directly explain the narrated change.
entries.hold_policy: Stop the spread at the semantic result. Do not pulse or continue bleeding during the reading phase.

transitions.semantic_trigger: Adjacent shots have no material reason to share a print process or need a clean editorial contrast.
transitions.action: Cut directly from the held result to the next fully established page state.
transitions.result_state: The next shot is immediately readable with its own single anchor.
transitions.hold_policy: No transition hold; allocate time to the destination content.

transitions.semantic_trigger: Two adjacent statements form a genuine ordered sequence and share one reading direction.
transitions.action: A single feed edge carries the outgoing page state off-frame and reveals the incoming page state without exposing fragments or empty staging.
transitions.result_state: The incoming page is stable, opaque, and owns one anchor.
transitions.hold_policy: Use only across the boundary; do not repeat for more than two adjacent transitions.

global_rules: All motion derives from deterministic local composition time and remains seek-safe.
Every action must name a print-process cause, a visible state change, and a stable readable result.
Use at most one main motion cause per shot and complete it before the reading hold.
No perpetual paper movement, grain animation, registration jitter, or decorative ink drift.
Simplify choreography when the fixed SRT window cannot contain Entry, Action, Result, Hold, and Exit.
Adjacent shots must differ on at least three variation axes, and anchor form or motion cause must differ on at least one.
A material process may animate only when that same process is inside the shot's two-item material budget.

Every shot freezes exactly one ordinary-primary asset in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order before authoring; HTML/CSS/SVG motion is auxiliary and cannot become the sole or primary material.
The ordinary-primary asset must contribute visible pixels in the result region throughout the readable hold.

modes.usage: The only supported output: one opaque 16:9 flat editorial page rendered directly in HyperFrames.
constraints: Keep the paper field opaque and full-frame.
Do not derive secondary compositing passes or staged spatial constructs.
Do not add burned-in subtitles or BGM.
All factual type remains real HTML/SVG content in the same source.
Bind exactly one ordinary-primary asset per shot in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order; native HTML/CSS/SVG remains auxiliary.
Record the ordinary-primary route, stable asset identity, provenance, and visible result-region contribution.
verification_requirements: Ordinary-primary route-order and frozen asset-identity check for every shot
Result-region pixel-contribution check proving the ordinary primary is visible and not replaced by native graphics
Current HyperFrames 16:9 decode and duration pass before promotion
Boundary, action, result, and hold frame inspection before promotion
Target-raster typography, contrast, and thumbnail-accent inspection before promotion

hard_rules: This profile is draft and calibration-only; never select it as a global default or claim production readiness without author calibration and current HyperFrames render evidence.
Use one opaque 16:9 flat page, exactly one routed ordinary-primary material, and exactly one semantic anchor per shot.

WFR compatibility invariant: for every shot, resolve and freeze the ordinary primary in immutable user-media → image-generation → Pexels order and record rejected earlier candidates when a later route is used.
Record the ordinary-primary route, stable asset identity, provenance, concrete material use, and measurable result-region pixel contribution before authoring.
HTML/CSS/SVG may provide factual typography, structure, marks, crop geometry, and auxiliary texture only; it may never be the sole or primary material.
Render every factual word, number, name, quotation, date, source, and unit as real HTML text or SVG text from approved content.

When image-generation is the ordinary-primary route, request a non-text paper, print, photo, scan, or specimen material and never ask it to create factual text, tables, numbers, logos, or document facsimiles.
Choose negative space from the low, medium, or high semantic-density band; do not apply one fixed sparse percentage to every shot.
Use exactly one high-chroma hue for one semantic role; prefer user, brand, or approved-media color evidence, otherwise require the Director to choose a content-driven hue and record the rationale.
Never substitute a default purple-blue gradient or add a second competing hue when no explicit user color is supplied.
Count the mandatory paper substrate as material-process one and select at most one additional reproduction process.
Derive the single main action from print causality and stop it before the readable hold.
Change at least three variation axes between adjacent shots; anchor form or motion cause must be one of the changes.
Do not copy upstream example images, sample wording, cultural labels, object recipes, or vertical poster proportions.
do: Extract one visual judgment from the fixed SRT before selecting an anchor.
Resolve user-media → image-generation → Pexels, freeze one ordinary-primary asset, and prove its visible pixel contribution before composing the shot.
Use real local typography as an auxiliary compositional system and a source-verifiable information carrier over the routed ordinary-primary material.
Let empty paper collect on one side or band according to the selected density tier.
Make the single accent visible at thumbnail scale without turning the frame commercially colorful, and record its evidence source or content-semantic rationale.
Use paper-feed, pressure, registration, screening, or absorption only when the physical behavior explains the semantic change.
Record density tier, anchor form, quadrant, type relation, accent form, material process, and motion cause for adjacent-difference review.
Omit microtext when no real secondary information exists.
dont: Do not imitate a vertical zine poster inside a 16:9 frame.
Do not use cultural or geographic style labels in place of observable design constraints.
Do not use a pure HTML/CSS/SVG page, procedural paper field, native SVG specimen, or type-only render as the sole or primary material.
Do not skip an available suitable user-media material in favor of image-generation or Pexels without recording the rejection reason.
Do not build a collage, sticker wall, scrapbook, glossy paper mockup, cinematic scene, or 3D paper object.
Do not treat random grain, torn edges, misregistration, or ink bleed as interchangeable decoration.
Do not combine paper, scan noise, halftone, misregistration, and ink bleed into a texture stack.
Do not fabricate archive dates, weather, locations, source numbers, quotations, or captions.
Do not repeat the tiny-photo plus color-dot plus archive-microtext recipe across a section.
Do not create variation by changing only hue, position, or copy.
Do not use unreadable raster text as evidence.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Bind whitespace and text capacity to the count of independent semantic facts instead of a fixed sparse-poster ratio.
constraints: Low uses 58%-72% negative space, medium 44%-58%, and high 30%-44%.
More than six independent facts requires a split shot or another profile.
Never shrink approved factual text below the target-raster readability threshold to preserve emptiness.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Choose the one semantic carrier that best expresses the sentence meaning while preserving the separately frozen ordinary-primary material.
constraints: Only one form may own the shot.
Every form still binds one ordinary-primary asset in user-media → image-generation → Pexels order.
If type-led, the routed paper, print, or scan material is ordinary primary and typography is the semantic focus; omit a second image subject.
For other forms, the routed photo, print, scan, or specimen asset is ordinary primary and HTML/SVG remains auxiliary.
An adjacent shot must change anchor form or motion cause.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Place the anchor so negative space directs reading and adjacent shots change visual weight.
constraints: Keep an approximate 5%-7% frame-edge breathing zone.
Do not use the same negative-space direction for three consecutive shots.
Changing quadrant alone does not satisfy adjacent difference.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Vary how real typography relates to the single anchor without sacrificing factual legibility.
constraints: All factual characters remain real HTML/SVG text.
Microtext may contain only real secondary information.
Do not repeat the same type relation and anchor form on adjacent shots.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Give the single high-chroma hue one concrete semantic job and a thumbnail-visible area.
constraints: Use one high-chroma hue only.
Prefer user, brand, or approved-media color evidence; if absent, record the Director's content-semantic rationale for the selected hue.
Never use a default purple-blue gradient or a second competing hue as the fallback.
Do not weaken the accent with global fading or low-saturation treatment.
Changing accent hue alone does not create a new composition.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Limit tactile character to a paper substrate plus at most one semantically motivated reproduction process.
constraints: The frozen ordinary-primary asset supplies the material source; HTML/CSS/SVG cannot substitute for it.
The total material-process count is at most two.
Paper-only means a routed ordinary-primary paper, print, or scan source with no added procedural defect; it never means a pure CSS/SVG paper texture.
If the ordinary-primary asset visibly contains scan, halftone, misregistration, or ink bleed, that embedded process consumes the optional second process and no additional defect may be added.
The optional process must be visible but subordinate to the semantic anchor.
Do not animate a process that is not selected.

adaptation_knobs.adaptation_goal: Select one physical print cause that explains the visible semantic change, or remain static when motion adds no meaning.
constraints: At most one main cause per shot.
Complete the action before the content-dependent hold.
Registration, halftone, and absorption require their matching selected material process.
Do not reuse the same cause on adjacent shots unless the SRT establishes one continuous action.

inspiration_atoms.adaptation: Compile each shot in an ordered sequence: observable identity and anti-identity, stable invariants, immutable ordinary-primary routing, semantic fit, density-banded attention geometry, one anchor, auxiliary real typography, single-accent logic, bounded material process, print-causal motion, then a quality gate. The method is adapted to 16:9 deterministic HyperFrames rather than copied as an image-generation prompt.
excluded_brand_expression: upstream skill name and callable syntax
upstream example prompts, captions, objects, dates, and recipes
upstream 3:5 output ratio and fixed sparse percentages
upstream instruction to invent in-image text

inspiration_atoms.adaptation: Separate invariant visual relationships from variation axes so the profile stays identifiable without repeating one composition. HyperFrames axes cover semantic density, anchor form, quadrant, type relation, accent form, material process, and motion cause.

Retain the relationship of subdued paper and secondary ink supporting one high-chroma semantic signal, while limiting the 16:9 moving profile to paper plus at most one reproduction defect. Motion is derived from the chosen print process and ends in a readable result.
excluded_brand_expression: upstream texture recipes copied as a set

signature_motifs.description: One frozen ordinary-primary paper, print, photo, scan, or specimen material supports a single approved statement, evidence fragment, or state imprint in a density-banded field; auxiliary real typography and one chromatic ink role make the conclusion verifiable.
signature_combination: one routed ordinary-primary material with visible pixel contribution
one semantic anchor with auxiliary real HTML/SVG factual typography

signature_motifs.description: One selected print cause changes the same routed ordinary-primary material and semantic anchor, then stops at a stable readable result, with paper and the optional process staying inside the two-item material budget.
signature_combination: same ordinary-primary asset and semantic anchor from entry through result
paper plus at most one optional reproduction process

exhausted_motifs.reason: The recurring tiny-photo plus color-dot plus archive-microtext recipe collapses variation into one recognizable template and often fabricates decorative metadata.
Misregistration is allowed only for correction, alignment, deviation, or normalization semantics and at most once per section.
Ink spread is not a default transition; it requires explicit spread, absorption, reach, or boundary-change meaning.
Repeated centered type-only shots remove semantic composition and turn the film into a slide template.
A full-bleed image removes the negative-space relationship and makes the paper treatment a superficial filter.
Fabricated dates, locations, identifiers, weather, or source lines cannot be used as editorial texture.
Factual text must remain verifiable HTML/SVG content and cannot be delegated to image generation or an unreadable raster.

conflicts_with.reason: Both may use paper and editorial text, but greenroom-writing depends on a studio world, multiple physical materials, and evidence-wall accumulation while quiet-editorial-print remains one flat page with one anchor.
conflicts_with.resolution: Choose one worldview for the entire shot. Borrow at most the concept of verified editorial annotation; do not import the studio, evidence wall, lamp, string, or object-stage grammar.

conflicts_with.reason: Both use a restrained accent, but gradient-flow treats chromatic movement as energy while quiet-editorial-print treats one opaque ink role and a physical print cause as evidence.
conflicts_with.resolution: Do not combine gradient sweeps with print defects. Select the template whose motion cause matches the narration.

borrowable_patterns.description: Choose negative-space and text capacity from low, medium, or high semantic density rather than applying a fixed minimal-poster ratio.
conditions: The borrowing template preserves every required fact at readable size.
The borrowing template defines its own material and color identity.
The density tier is recorded for review.

borrowable_patterns.description: Use one auxiliary print-like action over a routed ordinary-primary material only when its physical cause explains the semantic state change, then stop at a stable readable result.
conditions: The borrowing template has a compatible flat material system.
The borrowing shot freezes an ordinary-primary asset independently of native typography or graphics.
The action completes before the reading hold.
The selected process is included in the shot's material budget.

restrictions: No upstream example images, sample copy, sample objects, fonts, logos, or repository branding are included.
The 16:9 HyperFrames profile is an independent abstraction and does not claim affiliation or visual identity ownership.
Cultural or geographic style labels from upstream are excluded and replaced with observable constraints.

forbidden_materials: upstream example images and generated posters
upstream sample prompts, captions, dates, objects, and layout recipes copied verbatim
upstream repository branding and callable-skill expression
third-party fonts, photos, logos, marks, and product UI
absolute local paths, secrets, cookies, and private project copy

removed_categories: absolute paths and private runtime data
upstream example images and bitmap outputs
upstream sample copy, objects, captions, and prompts
upstream brand expression and callable syntax
fixed vertical ratio and sample-specific measurements

stale_rules.original_claim: Use a fixed 3:5 vertical poster with 70%-90% negative space and a small 8%-25% cluster.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: Those values belong to the upstream vertical raster-poster task. This profile derives 16:9 whitespace and anchor ranges from semantic-density tiers and requires target-raster verification.

stale_rules.original_claim: The bitmap prompt may invent a short phrase and optional date, location, weather, or signature for the composition.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: HyperFrames factual content must come from SRT, user material, or approved copy and must render as real HTML/SVG text. Fabricated archive metadata and image-generated fact text are prohibited.

stale_rules.original_claim: A cultural or geographic zine label may define the desired mood.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: Style selection must be expressed through observable composition, typography, palette, material, and motion constraints rather than cultural labels.

stale_rules.original_claim: Default delivery is a generated raster image.
stale_rules.isolation_reason: This profile compiles editable deterministic HyperFrames source but still freezes one ordinary-primary asset per shot. Resolve user-media first, use image-generation second for non-text paper/print/photo/scan/specimen material, and use Pexels third; HTML/SVG remains auxiliary and image generation cannot own factual typography.
